findings.title: Date override path skips busy-time checks
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot is not rejected by the override bounds, the function returns true before executing the busy.every check. Existing bookings and calendar busy times inside date overrides are therefore ignored, which can allow double bookings.

findings.title: Day.js objects are compared with ===
findings.body: The code checks dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...). Day.js instances are objects, so === compares identity and is always false. The intended start-equals-end unavailable-date case is never detected, which can incorrectly mark slots as available.

findings.title: Multiple date overrides on the same day are handled incorrectly
findings.body: checkIfIsAvailable uses dateOverrides.find and returns true from the callback as soon as the slot is outside a same-day override. If a user has multiple date overrides on the same day, a slot inside a later override but outside the first one will be rejected. The logic should check whether the slot is contained in at least one override instead of rejecting on the first non-matching override.

findings.title: Date override containment ignores slot boundaries
findings.body: The date override check only rejects slots that end before the override starts or start after the override ends. It does not require slotStartTime >= override start and slotEndTime <= override end. Slots that overlap the beginning or end of a date override are therefore treated as available.

findings.title: Working-hours check ignores event end time and misuses find
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, end is computed from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, so event length is ignored and slots extending past working hours can pass. Additionally, workingHours.find returns true if any same-day working-hours range does not contain the slot, so multiple ranges can reject a valid slot, and if no range matches the day the code falls through and may return true.

findings.title: Date override date matching uses inconsistent timezone handling
findings.body: checkIfIsAvailable computes utcOffset from dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone), then applies it to dayjs(date.start), which is parsed in the server's local timezone, and formats it while slotStartTime is UTC. On a server not set to UTC, the YYYY MM DD comparison can mismatch, causing date overrides to be missed or misapplied.

findings.title: Timezone adjustment for date overrides drops day shifts
findings.body: When converting date overrides to minutes, the code adds the timezone offset and then takes only hour() and minute(). If the offset moves the override across midnight, the day shift is discarded. Combined with the activeOverrides filter that does not account for the shifted date, overrides can be generated on the wrong invitee day for large timezone differences.

findings.title: No regression test for round-robin fixed-host date overrides
findings.body: The PR description says it fixes date overrides for fixed hosts in round-robin events, but the added test only covers a personal event date override in a different attendee timezone. There is no automated test creating a round-robin event with a fixed host and asserting that slots outside the fixed host's date override are removed.
